tagline: Up the Green Bay shore on an old single-file trail.
intro: M-35 leaves Menominee at a Y-shaped corner by John Henes Park and heads northeast along the shore of Green Bay toward Escanaba, the closest highway to the water. At the Delta County line it passes from Central to Eastern time. From Escanaba it runs with US 2 and US 41 over the mouth of the Escanaba River and along Little Bay de Noc to Gladstone, 64 miles in all.
Much of the way it lies over the Sault and Green Bay Trail, a Native American footpath 12 to 18 inches wide. Traffic went single file.

moments.title: Cedar River
moments.text: A community at the mouth of the Cedar River on Green Bay, begun with a sawmill in 1854, with Wells State Park just to the south.

moments.title: Sand Point Lighthouse, Escanaba
moments.text: First lit in 1868 to warn ships off the sand shoals, and restored since, it was built with its tower facing the land instead of the water, and nobody knows whether on purpose.

moments.title: Gladstone
moments.text: Settled in 1859 as a port for shipping iron ore, it became a rail hub once the mine that fed it was worked out, and the byway ends here as M-35 turns inland.

sources.label: MDOT, Pure Michigan Byways Driving Guide (Wayback Machine snapshot, December 2025)
